newsitem.title: USA: Dialogic sees disappointing earnings, stock falls.
newsitem.headline: Dialogic sees disappointing earnings, stock falls.

text.p: Dialogic Corp., which makes parts used in computer voice, fax and data applications, said Thursday it expects disappointing results in the first quarter, sparking a sharp sell-off in its stock.
The stock slid $7.265, or more than 26 percent to $20 early on Nasdaq.
Dialogic said current data show it is likely to have first-quarter sales of $54 million to $57 million, resulting in earnings falling below analysts' estimate of 31 cents a share.
In the fourth quarter ended Dec. 31, the Parsippany, N.J.-based company earned $5.6 million, or 34 cents a share, on revenues of $59.4 million.

Dialogic said it operates on little or no backlog and a significant amount of its orders are typically received and shipped within a day. Because of this, sales for the quarter cannot be accurately determined until the period ends, it said.
Dialogic said the year started more slowly than the company had anticipated, but expenses have so far been in line with expectations for the quarter.

Dialogic is a leading manufacturer of computer telephony components are used in voice, fax, data, voice recognition, speech synthesis and call centre management applications. It has regional headquarters in Tokyo and Brussels and sales offices worldwide.
